shots.say: What can an elephant's trunk do?
Is it a nose? A hand? A shower?
I'm Milo. Let's find out together!
Welcome to The Animated Zoo, friends!
Today we fly to the sunny savanna.
Here we are! Look who is waiting for us.
This is Tumble. Tumble is a baby elephant.
And this is Tumble's mama. Hello, Mama!
Look at Tumble's long, bendy trunk.
A trunk is a nose.
And it is an upper lip, too. All in one!
Where is your nose? Can you touch your nose?
At the tip of the trunk are two little holes.
An elephant breathes through them. Sniff, sniff!
Sniff, sniff! Tumble smells something yummy.
An elephant uses its trunk to smell its food.
It can even smell water from far, far away!
So, is a trunk a nose, or a tail?
A nose! A very, very long nose.
Now Tumble is hungry. Look, a fruit!
A trunk is like a hand, too.
It can grab, hold, pick up and reach.
Yum, yum, yum! Can you munch like Tumble?
Here comes Mama. Her trunk is very, very strong.
It can lift a big, heavy log. Up it goes!
And a trunk is very gentle, too.
It can pick up one tiny piece of straw.
So strong, and so gentle. What a nose!
There are no bones inside a trunk.
So it can bend this way, and that way!
Can you wiggle your arm like a trunk? Wiggle, wiggle!
That is two trunk jobs. One, smell. Two, grab.
Phew, it is hot! Tumble and Mama walk into the river.
Time for a drink. Watch Mama's trunk!
She sucks the water up into her trunk. Slurp!
Does the water go all the way up her nose? Yes, or no?
No! The water only goes part of the way up.
Then she curls her trunk to her mouth,
and blows the water in! Glug, glug, glug.
So a trunk is not like a straw. It carries the water to the mouth.
Now it is Tumble's turn. His trunk is still short.
Baby elephants are clumsy with their trunks at first.
Oops! Splash! The water goes everywhere.
But Tumble keeps trying. Little by little, he learns.
Can you slurp like an elephant? Slurp, slurp!
A baby elephant drinks his mama's milk with his mouth.
So he does not need a long trunk yet.
Now Mama fills her trunk again. What will she do?
Whoosh! A shower! She sprays water all over her back.
Elephants squirt cool water over their bodies to keep cool.
Tumble wants a shower too. Ready, steady, spray!
Can you spray like an elephant? Whoosh, whoosh!
Now we have four trunk jobs. Three, drink. Four, spray.
Now Tumble wades into the deep, deep water.
Deeper, and deeper, and deeper.
Where did Tumble go? Can you see him?
Peekaboo! There is the tip of his trunk.
An elephant can use its trunk like a snorkel.
The tip stays up in the air, so he can breathe.
Only the tip of the trunk is above the water.
Breathe in through your nose. And out. Can you do it?
Tumble walks along under the water. Bubble, bubble!
Let's count his bubbles. One, two, three!
And out he comes. Drip, drip, drip!
Tumble flaps his big ears. Flap, flap, flap!
What did Tumble breathe with? His trunk, or his tail?
His trunk! Just like a snorkel.
The sun goes down. Tumble walks home with Mama.
Tumble is tired. He comes close to Mama.
Mama reaches out her trunk, and strokes him gently.
Elephants stroke each other with their trunks.
It is like a hug. A trunk hug!
Can you give yourself a big hug? Squeeze!
Tumble feels warm and happy.
Five, snorkel. Six, hug. Six trunk jobs!
One nose, six jobs. Wow!
Time to remember what we learned!
Is a trunk a nose? Yes, or no?
Yes! A nose and an upper lip, all in one.
Are there bones inside a trunk? Yes, or no?
No bones! It bends this way and that way.
What does Tumble use as a snorkel?
His trunk!
One nose, six jobs. Let's count them!
Smell, grab, drink,
spray, snorkel, hug!
Good night, Tumble. Good night, Mama.
Thank you for learning with me, friends. See you at the zoo!
